newsitem.title: USA: Banc One says First USA merger still on.
newsitem.headline: Banc One says First USA merger still on.

text.p: Banc One Corp said on Thursday an earnings restatement by First USA Inc will not serve as a basis for terminating the proposed merger between Banc One and First USA.

Banc One said it has reviewed the restatement announced earlier Thursday. Banc One said the restatement reflected the adoption of two accounting policies made in anticipation of the merger. The accounting changes have no impact on net income previously reported by First USA for fiscal years 1995 and 1996, although net income for fiscal 1994 increased $48 million, Banc One said.

Banc One said one accouting change conformed the accounting treatment of marketing expense of First USA to the practice of Banc One. Specifically, First USA amortized marketing expense over a 12-month period, while Banc One reported marketing expense in the period incurred.

The second change was required to effect the historic adoption of recording gains on securitizaton of credit card receivables prior to January 1, 1997, Banc One said. As a result of this action, a new asset in the amount of $271 million appears on the restated First USA balance sheet as of December 31, 1996.
Banc One said the $271 million asset will be fully reduced over calendar year 1997 and will not affect 1998.

For the three months ended March 31, 1997 this reduction of the new asset adversely impacted First USA's reported earnings by $53 million and will reduce earnings by a total of $176 million for the 12 months ended December 31, 1997.
The amortization of the accounting entry will not affect cash earnings per share of either First USA or Banc One and will have no adverse effect upon capital, Banc One said.
"We remain extremely pleased with the operating trends and business prospects of First USA," Banc One chairman and chief executive John McCoy said in a statement.

"We fully anticipate First USA will meet or exceed the earnings projections made at the time the acquisition was announced, excluding the effect of the second accounting change. Further, we have every confidence that 1998 reported earnings will meet our earlier projections and expect the merger will close by the end of the second quarter."
